pages.title: SC on SIR — ECI can examine but not decide citizenship

facts.text: Case: Association for Democratic Reforms v. Election Commission of India
facts.head: Verdict

facts.text: Upheld: ECI order for Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls — conducted before November 2025 Bihar Assembly elections
facts.head: Verdict

facts.text: Held: SIR broadly proportionate; ECI is best placed to decide method of revision
facts.head: Verdict

facts.text: Citizenship: ECI may examine citizenship prima facie and contextually (for electoral roll only)
facts.head: Verdict

facts.text: ⚠ ECI cannot finally declare a person a non-citizen — deletion from roll ≠ loss of citizenship
facts.head: Verdict

facts.text: Referral: doubtful cases go to competent authority under Citizenship Act, 1955 — decide preferably before the next election in that constituency
facts.head: Verdict

facts.text: Presumption: name on roll gives only an evidentiary presumption of citizenship, not absolute
facts.head: Verdict

facts.text: Aadhaar accepted as proof of identity
facts.head: Safeguards ordered

facts.text: Deleted voters' names published with reasons; opportunity of hearing; judicial officers assist hearings
facts.head: Safeguards ordered

pages.title: Right to be forgotten vs open justice

facts.text: Trigger: Delhi High Court order of 29 May 2026 on limited online discoverability of judicial records
facts.head: News

facts.text: Right to be forgotten: removal / de-indexing of outdated personal info — called right to erasure in European law (GDPR)
facts.head: News

facts.text: Linked to: informational privacy under Article 21 — ⚠ not absolute
facts.head: News

facts.text: DPDP Act, 2023: recognises right to erasure; application to court records unclear
facts.head: News

facts.text: Delhi HC (Justice Sachin Datta): recognised RTBF as part of privacy under Article 21; search engines may delist judgments linked to a name — mainly for acquitted persons, private civil disputes, non-parties
facts.head: News

facts.text: Case: Rajagopal v. State of TN (1994); Holding: Right to be let alone; court records open to comment
facts.head: Key cases

facts.text: Case: K.S. Puttaswamy v. UoI (2017); Holding: Privacy a fundamental right; informational privacy
facts.head: Key cases

facts.text: Case: Dharamraj Bhanushankar Dave v. State of Gujarat (2017); Holding: Gujarat HC denied removal of acquittal details
facts.head: Key cases

facts.text: Case: Orissa HC (2020); Holding: Online sexual abuse — called for debate on RTBF
facts.head: Key cases

facts.text: Case: Delhi HC (2021); Holding: Allowed limited removal from search results
facts.head: Key cases

facts.text: Case: Supreme Court (2022); Holding: Registry to remove a couple's details (marital dispute) from search engines
facts.head: Key cases

facts.text: Case: Kerala HC (2023); Holding: RTBF not automatic for ongoing proceedings
facts.head: Key cases

facts.text: Case: Indian Kanoon matter (2024); Holding: Warned obfuscation harms public record
facts.head: Key cases

facts.text: PYQ: Right to Privacy — Article 21 and Part III freedoms
facts.head: Key cases

facts.text: First: amends Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Rules, 2011 — registration tied to purposes from a Schedule of 105 permissible purposes; States/UTs of operation specified; existing NGOs get one year to choose

facts.text: Key functionary: widened (directors, partners, trustees, Karta of HUF, etc.)

facts.text: Disclosures: social-media accounts, official website, ultimate/original donors (even for routed donations), donor-advised funds
